lens: Blind first-pass cryptanalysis: corpus statistics on the rune transcription (13,041 ciphertext runes, 56 pages + 1 plaintext page) cross-checked against the page scans and byte-level forensics of the released image corpus. Everything below was measured in /tmp/lp_blind/material; scratch work in /tmp/lp_blind/scratch-cryptanalyst/.
observations: WHAT THE OBJECT IS: krisyotam_runes.txt holds 57 %-separated pages; pages 0-55 are ciphertext (13,041 runes over the 29-rune futhorc, word dividers '-', sentence dots '.', line marks '/'), page 56 reads as direct plaintext with no key: 'PARABLE. LIKE THE INSTAR TUNNELING TO THE SURFACE. WE MUST SHED OUR OWN CIRCUMFERENCES. FIND THE DIVINITY WITHIN AND EMERGE.' - this calibrates the transcription alphabet and proves the corpus ends in clear.

CENTRAL ANOMALY (my strongest finding): adjacent identical runes are suppressed ~5x. 88 doublets observed vs ~450 expected (kappa at shift 1 = 0.196; >15 sigma). Everything else is flat: unigram IoC = 0.9998 (uniform), kappa at every shift 2..109 ~ 1.0, chi2 of rune frequencies flat. The suppression is equally present within words (0.63%), across word breaks (0.84%), across line breaks (0.74%), on every one of the 56 pages, and is spread over 28 of 29 runes (only ᛒ B never doubles). The first-difference stream C[i+1]-C[i] mod 29 is uniform over 1..28 with ONLY 0 suppressed (0.68% vs 3.45%), and its IoC is 1.024 - this kills simple autokey / cumulative-sum-of-plaintext models (those would give diff-IoC ~1.7). The ciphertext behaves exactly like 'uniform random conditioned on no immediate repeat'.

No periodicity, no key reuse: Kasiski/kappa null at all tested shifts; aligned-kappa between all 1,540 page pairs, all chapter pairs (chapters delimited by the transcription's '&'/'$' marks: 9 blocks of 3,5,8,7,4,6,7,15,1 pages), and all 18 '&'-sections shows zero significant coincidence spikes. Whatever the key is, it never visibly repeats across 13k runes.

Despite OTP-like flatness there ARE long repeats: a 7-gram ᛞᛄᚢ|ᛒᛖᛁ|ᚫ with identical word-boundary pattern occurs on page 27 (position 28, immediately after the red drop-cap section opening) and at the very END of page 54 (where the alternate transcription shows it terminated by the heavy section mark ⁜). Chance probability including the boundary match << 1e-3. A second repeated 5-gram ᛒᛗᚱᚾᛗ occurs word-internally on p22 and as a standalone word on p48; a third 5-gram repeats between p28 and p33. Gaps (6395, 6553, 1031) share no common factor - not classical period evidence.

Word structure is preserved and odd: 3,344 words, mean 3.9 runes, 9.6% single-rune words (English runic plaintext like the parable page runs ~4.75 mean, ~4% one-letter words). First-letter and last-letter distributions of words are uniform (chi2 38.4 / 33.3, df 28) - no structure leaks at word edges.

A lone Arabic numeral '7' sits inline in the ciphertext of page 10 ('ᚩᚦᛏ-7-ᚷ-...') - confirmed in BOTH independent transcriptions (krisyotam_runes.txt and page-images/p8-14.txt) and visually verified in page-images/p10.jpg (the page with the branching-tree drawing). Pages 36-38 additionally carry numerals 1-5 as numbered-list markers.

Byte forensics: released page image 'cijhho123/2014/Liber Primus/liber primus images full/05.jpg' carries a 336,713-byte BYTE-REVERSED trailer after the JPEG EOI containing (a) a full 2400x3600 page scan and (b) an ASCII block giving a 5x5 magic square: rows [272,138,341,131,151],[366,199,130,320,18],[226,245,91,245,226],[18,320,130,199,366],[151,131,341,138,272] - every row, column and diagonal sums to 1033, and the layout is a 180-degree palindrome. The embedded page interleaves these numbers with English rune-words; I verified cell (3,3): ᚠᚩᚱᛗ = FORM = 2+7+11+71 = 91 under the prime gematria (F=2,U=3,TH=5,O=7,...,EA=109), exactly the number it replaces, and identical rune-words recur in cells carrying equal numbers. So the authors demonstrably operate on word-level PRIME-GEMATRIA SUMS, and 1033 is a canonical constant (cf. released-artifacts/2015-1033/ onion dumps named '1033adacic').

More hidden-byte inventory (TRAILING-DATA.json, verified on disk): 10.jpg/onion6.jpg carry an identical 3.49MB JPEG trailer; Huh2.jpg and Outt.png carry trailers; page-images/0_wisdom.jpg itself carries a 72,700-byte byte-reversed (truncated) JPEG of the same 'wisdom' page - byte-reversal is a recurring Cicada stego idiom in this corpus.

The book's presentation layer is lossy in the main transcription: red ink marks giant illuminated drop-caps opening sections (pages p0,3,6,7,8,15,23,27,33,39,40,53,54 measured by red-pixel scan); the alternate in-material transcriptions (p8-14.txt, p54-55.txt) preserve a punctuation HIERARCHY (• word, ⁘ clause, ⁚, ⁜ heavy section) and margin dot-clusters (p54 has ':'':' left margin and a three-dot triangle right margin) - all collapsed to '-'/'.' in krisyotam_runes.txt. Neither color, drop-cap status, margin marks, nor punctuation weight survives into the file most attacks would be run on.

Released-corpus anchors: one single RSA-4096 key (6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F) signs 137 valid messages 2012-2017; among signed payloads is a 991-byte high-entropy 'liber-primus-hash-block' (a signed commitment to the LP) plus two 991-byte outguess blobs - the authors cryptographically committed to this text, which argues the pages are meaningful ciphertext rather than filler.

Page 49 (66 runes) has the flattest IoC in the book (0.825, below random expectation) and page 54 shows IoC 1.099; the short section-final pages (49,50,54,55) are the best low-cost attack targets because their sections are single-screen units.

hypotheses.title: The encryption mechanism is a 29-state device/chain that MUST step at every rune (no-stay rule): ciphertext is uniform-random-conditioned-on-no-adjacent-repeat
hypotheses.motivation: Measured on krisyotam_runes.txt pages 0-55: doublets 88 vs 450 expected (>15 sigma), suppression uniform across pages/word-breaks/line-breaks and across 28 of 29 runes; first-difference distribution uniform on 1..28 with only 0 suppressed; diff-IoC 1.024 rules out plaintext-fed autokey and cumulative-sum models; kappa flat at all lags rules out periodic keys. The one model class that reproduces ALL of this is a pointer/wheel cipher whose state must move each step (e.g., C_i = C_{i-1} + s_i with s_i in 1..28 carrying the message+key), or an explicit re-draw-on-repeat rule in keystream generation.
hypotheses.first_test: Fit the exact statistics: compare observed inter-repeat gap distribution and the 88 surviving doublets against (a) hard-exclusion Markov (predicts 0 doublets - already falsified, so) (b) partial-rejection models (~80% rejection), and (c) 'step = prime(P_i)+k mod 29' wheel models where only specific plaintext runes can produce step 0 - check whether the doubled-rune contexts share a recoverable property. Scorable in minutes on /tmp/lp_blind/material/krisyotam_runes.txt.

hypotheses.title: Word-level prime-gematria sums are the operative cipher layer, keyed by the book's own constants (1033, the magic square, 7)
hypotheses.motivation: The reversed trailer I extracted from released 05.jpg proves the authors equate rune-words with their prime-gematria sums (verified FORM=91; identical words in equal-numbered cells; all lines sum 1033, square is a 180-degree palindrome - same symmetry group as the book's facing-page art). The cipher corpus has preserved word units with uniform letter stats but non-English length distribution (9.6% one-rune words), consistent with words being VALUE-carriers rather than letter-sequences. A literal '7' sits inline on page 10 and numerals 1-5 on pages 36-38 - numbers are first-class citizens of the ciphertext.
hypotheses.first_test: Compute gematria sums (prime values and mod-29 residues) of all 3,344 cipher words; test for arithmetic structure: sums mod 29/59/1033 distribution, per-line and per-page totals (do any pages/lines sum to 1033 or 3301?), and whether the 320 one-rune words function as numeric separators/operators.

hypotheses.title: The published runes are not the raw ciphertext: a presentation-layer rule (scribal avoidance or homophone swap on repeat) was applied when the book was drawn
hypotheses.motivation: The no-doublet rule holds across line breaks and even across the '&' section marks - exactly what a scribe/typesetter applying 'never draw the same rune twice in a row' would produce, and the 88 exceptions are scattered randomly (28 different runes). If true, attacks on the transcription fail subtly no matter the cipher. The corpus gives a ground-truth control: the solved-era pages (images exist in released-artifacts/cijhho123/2014/Liber Primus/liber primus images full/) have known plaintext and known cipher.
hypotheses.first_test: Transcribe (or locate in-material transcriptions of) the solved pages and measure THEIR ciphertext doublet rate. If solved pages double at normal rates, the suppression is specific to the unsolved cipher (supports H1); if they are also suppressed, a book-wide presentation rule exists and every doubled position in the images deserves glyph-level scrutiny (crops of the 88 surviving doublets in p*.jpg).

hypotheses.title: The repeated 7-gram ties section START (p27) to section END (p54): the keystream re-enters the same state at structural boundaries - sections, not pages, are the cryptographic unit
hypotheses.motivation: Measured: ᛞᛄᚢ-ᛒᛖᛁ(-ᚫ) repeats with identical word boundaries at p27 pos 28 (right after the red drop-cap ᛗ opening a section, cicada-wing page) and at the very end of p54 (terminated by the heavy ⁜ mark per p54-55.txt; p54 is also a drop-cap page with marginal dot clusters). Chance < 1e-3. Two further 5-gram repeats (p22/p48, p28/p33). The '&'/'$' marks define 18 sections; red drop-caps mark their openings.
hypotheses.first_test: For every section opening and ending, extract the first/last 10 runes and run pairwise delta-matching (exact and constant-shift-equivalent); also test whether distance-from-section-start reproduces any repeat alignment (keystream reset at '&' boundaries) - my page-aligned and section-START-aligned kappas were null, but END-aligned and offset-aligned variants are untested.

hypotheses.title: Key material is in the illustrations and margins, not the runes: dot clusters, branch forks, and page art encode numbers the text consumes
hypotheses.motivation: Verified stego habit: byte-reversed JPEG+magic-square inside 05.jpg; reversed JPEG inside page-images/0_wisdom.jpg; 3.49MB trailer in 10.jpg; outguess blobs signed by the master key (signed-payloads/*.bin). On-page: p54 carries two 2-dot clusters (left margin) and a 3-dot triangle (right margin) that no transcription records; p10's tree has a countable fork structure and sits on the page with the inline '7'; p27 has a detached cicada wing. The authors demonstrably put load-bearing data where only the images show it.
hypotheses.first_test: Systematic visual inventory over all 56 p*.jpg: margin dot-clusters, branch/fork counts, wing-vein counts, and positions of illustrations relative to text; emit as a per-page number vector and test it as shift/key against that page's runes (score with English runic trigrams from the parable + solved-page language model).

hypotheses.title: Re-transcription is a prerequisite: the standard transcription is lossy in ways that can break any correct attack
hypotheses.motivation: Direct diffs within the material: p8-14.txt and p54-55.txt preserve a punctuation hierarchy (• / ⁘ / ⁚ / ⁜) and show krisyotam collapsed all of it to '.'; red drop-caps and ink color are unrecorded; the inline '7' is nearly invisible in a text file; image file p54.jpg corresponds to krisyotam page 53 (off-by-one mapping drift somewhere mid-book, i.e., at least one image/transcription misalignment). If the cipher uses sentence- or section-keyed state (H4), wrong punctuation weight = wrong key schedule.
hypotheses.first_test: Build a full-fidelity transcription from the 56 p*.jpg scans (runes + color + punctuation weight + drop-caps + margin marks + numerals), diff it against krisyotam_runes.txt, and fix the page-numbering drift; rerun the entire statistical battery on the corrected text.

hypotheses.title: The plaintext under the final layer is not raw English but already-transformed material (gematria digits, or a second cipher text), explaining uniform letters WITH real word structure
hypotheses.motivation: Word lengths (mean 3.9, 9.6% single-rune words, max 14) do not match English-in-runes (parable: mean 4.75), yet word-edge statistics are perfectly uniform and sentence structure (headings like 'ᚫᛄ-ᛟᛋᚱ.' opening pages, 1-5 numbered lists on p36-38) is intact. A base-29 numeral encoding or a doubly-enciphered text would show exactly this: real segmentation, flat symbol stats.
hypotheses.first_test: Test the 320 one-rune words and 631 two-rune words as a numeral system: distribution of leading runes of short words vs a Benford-like or base-29 digit model; and test the numbered-list pages 36-38 (items 1-5) for per-item internal structure, since list items give known semantic parallelism.

hypotheses.title: Page 49 and the short section-final pages are a different regime (possibly key/checksum pages rather than prose)
hypotheses.motivation: Measured: p49 has 66 runes with IoC 0.825 (flatter than random - consistent with a deliberately all-distinct-ish sequence like key material), ends a section alone; pages 50/54/55 are the other sub-100-rune pages, all section/chapter ends per the '&'/'$' structure; p55's diff-IoC (0.882) is also sub-random. In the 2014 solved material, short special pages carried keys/hashes (the signed 991-byte liber-primus-hash-block shows the authors commit to hashes).
hypotheses.first_test: Treat p49's 66 runes as key material: use it (values, prime values, cumulative sums) as a trial keystream against the other short pages and against section openings; also check p49 for near-pangram structure (how many of the 29 runes appear exactly 2-3 times vs multinomial expectation).

lens: Forensic document examiner — physical/typographic/image layer: how the object was made, what marks carry information, and which measured anomalies in THIS material constrain the cipher.
observations: DOUBLET DEPLETION (the single strongest statistic in the corpus): the 56 unsolved pages (krisyotam_runes.txt segs 0-55, 13,041 runes) contain only 88 adjacent identical-rune pairs vs ~450 expected for a flat stream (~17 sigma). Depletion holds BOTH within words (64/10,088 pairs = 1/157) and across word boundaries (24/2,952 = 1/123), so it is a letter-stream property, not orthography. Zero triples. The anomaly is surgical: match rates at lags 2-30 are all ~450 (uniform), the successive-difference distribution mod 29 is uniform for all 28 nonzero values (chi2 41.7, df 27) and depressed ONLY at diff=0. Control test: glyph-cluster OCR (no transcription needed) of the SOLVED section (cijhho123 'liber primus images full' 01-16) gives 63 same-class adjacent pairs / 2,160 ≈ 1/34 ≈ uniform — the depletion is specific to the unsolved section's cipher, i.e. a method signature, not a house style.

THE PAGES ARE BORN-DIGITAL RENDERS, NOT SCANS: the vine borders of p40-p55 are pixel-identical across all 16 pages (0 pixels differing >80 in the margin zones); the two mid-border dot clusters (3 dots left at x≈367-425,y≈1498-1534; 5 dots right at x≈1975-2033) repeat at exact coordinates on every page. Rune glyphs are font stamps: on p17, 150 same-bounding-box glyph pairs are pixel-identical. All 56 canonical pages are 2400x3600 JFIF+ICC with the same header. Margin-ink density stratifies the book into design bands (p0-2 / p3-7 / p8-14[recto-verso alternation 44693/44805] / p15-21 none / p22 / p24-26 / p27-39 none / p40-55 vines) matching the chapter groupings of the per-section transcriptions (p0-2.txt, p3-7.txt, ..., p54-55.txt).

THE COMMON TRANSCRIPTION SILENTLY DROPS NON-RUNE PAYLOADS. Verified against page images: (a) p15 carries a 4x4 Arabic-numeral grid (3258 3222 3152 3038 / 3278 3299 3298 2838 / 3288 3294 3296 2472 / 4516 1206 708 1820) in which 14 of 16 cells equal 3301 minus a prime (43,79,149,263 / 23,2,3,463 / 13,7,5,829 / -,-,2593,1481), and the single cell 3299 (=3301-2, and 2 is the gematria value of rune F, the solved pages' interrupter) is printed in RED while all others are black; (b) p49-p51 carry a 272-entry two-character alphanumeric table (11+14+9 rows x 8 cols; first char always 0-4, second 0-9a-zA-Z — base-62-like values < ~310); (c) full-book page 73 (not in the p0-55 set) carries a 125-hex-digit block between rune paragraphs plus 5 identical 69-70px black dots in a zigzag (W-like) scatter at (1104,2448),(874,2517),(1604,2687),(922,2708),(1408,2748); (d) p53 has a red UP-ARROW glyph immediately before a 51-glyph all-red closing passage of the ch.40-53 chapter; (e) quotation marks (10 '"' chars = 5 quoted spans in p40-53.txt, 2 in p3-7.txt, 2 in p15-22.txt), apostrophes (4 across the book) and '⁚' colons occur inside the ciphertext; (f) literal Arabic numerals occur inline: a black '7' as a standalone word on p10, red list numerals 1-5 on p36-p38; (g) p37 is headed by two groups of cuneiform-style signs; (h) small infinity lemniscates appear on p0 (above the text) and p15 (below the grid).

RED INK IS A SEMANTIC LAYER: red dropcap+first-words on chapter openers (p0 dropcap S, p15, p40 and p54 dropcap F, full-74 parable dropcap P), a red final sentence closing ch.40-53 (p53, 51 glyphs), the red 3299 grid cell, red list numerals, and TWO DISTINCT red punctuation marks that transcriptions conflate: a 13-dot mark (common, section ends) vs a 10-dot mark occurring ONLY on p36, p38, p49 — exactly the numbered-list and table pages.

STREAM IS OTHERWISE PERFECTLY FLAT: all 29 runes occur 400-493 times (near-uniform), per-page normalized IoC 0.93-1.04 for every unsolved page, no periodic IoC in ciphertext or difference stream for any period 2-60, word-length distribution English-like (mean 4.42, 2,953 words), 181 sentence marks. Only the final parable segment reads as plaintext (IoC 1.82, 'PARABLE. LIKE THE INSTAR...').

PROVENANCE/COMPLETENESS: p0-p55 = pages 17-72 of the 75-page cijhho123 'liber primus images full' set (md5 of 17.jpg == p0.jpg); pages 73 (hex block + 5-dot scatter) and 74 (parable with dissolving-cicada art) are MISSING from the p-set and from krisyotam's page breaks near the end (krisyotam segs 49-56 do not align 1:1 with images; its seg 50 has 92 runes while image p50 is table-only). The Hadyn onion mirror is incomplete (51 files, 54.jpg truncated at 212,992 bytes).

MIRROR-LEVEL TRAILING DATA (from TRAILING-DATA.json, verified on-disk): cijhho123 LP '05.jpg' carries 336,713 appended bytes of nibble-shifted ASCII hex encoding a spaced columnar number table; '10.jpg' is two concatenated JPEGs (identical to onion6.jpg, 4,240,957 bytes total); the canonical 2012 1CcV1.jpg carries the known 61-byte 'TIBERIVS CLAVDIVS CAESAR' trailer. 137/140 PGP-signed artifacts verify against the single Cicada key (REPORT-A.md), so the canonical page set is signature-anchored.

Art-layer narrative: insect metamorphosis progresses through the book (mayfly + sapling p14, deliberately BLURRED tree p32 — the only blurred art object in the book, ghost tree + adult cicada p55, dissolving cicada on 74), suggesting page art encodes sequence/state rather than decoration.

hypotheses.title: The unsolved cipher is chained/differenced: the message rides on successive differences d[i]=ct[i]-ct[i-1] mod 29 (or equivalently ct is a running sum), with a near-never-zero increment
hypotheses.motivation: Measured on krisyotam_runes.txt segs 0-55: 88 doublets vs 450 expected (17 sigma), depletion present across word boundaries (24/2,952), confined EXACTLY to lag-1/diff-0 while all 28 nonzero successive differences are uniform (chi2 41.7, df 27) and lags 2-30 are uniform; zero triples. Glyph-cluster OCR control on solved pages 01-16 shows NO depletion (63/2,160 ≈ uniform). Only a construction of the form ct[i]=ct[i-1]+s[i] with s rarely 0 produces this signature while leaving every other statistic flat.
hypotheses.first_test: Rebuild the stream from images (restart chain per page and per line, both conventions), compute d[i], and run the entire solved-page toolkit on d instead of ct: shift, Atbash, Vigenere, and prime/totient streams with F-interrupter; score with runeglish n-grams. Also test the interrupter variant where the 88 doublet positions (s=0) mark plaintext-interrupter events.

hypotheses.title: The 88 doublet positions are themselves a deliberate low-rate channel (the analog of the solved pages' F-interrupter)
hypotheses.motivation: 88/13,041 = 0.68 percent — same order as the solved section's rare-interrupter rate; the doubled runes are spread over 37 pages with near-uniform rune identity (max 7 of any one rune), and gaps are Poisson-like (min 6, mean 148) — i.e. inserted events, not linguistic residue.
hypotheses.first_test: Extract the ordered 88-tuple of (page, offset, rune); test the rune sequence as a message (direct gematria letters, indices mod 29), test the position sequence (differences, mod page-length, against primes/totients), and test whether removing those 88 runes before decryption changes d-stream statistics.

hypotheses.title: The p15 4x4 grid is the key schedule in worked-example form: subtract from 3301 to recover a prime stream; the red cell 3299 (=3301-2=F) names the interrupter/origin
hypotheses.motivation: Measured from p15.jpg: 14 of 16 cells equal 3301 minus a prime (2,3,5,7,13,23,43,79,149,263,463,829,1481,2593); the only RED number in any grid is 3299, whose complement 2 is rune F's gematria prime — F was the solved pages' plaintext interrupter. Two cells (4516, 1206) break the pattern and need full-res re-reading. The grid sits on a chapter-opening page under a red header and above an infinity lemniscate (second lemniscate is on p0).
hypotheses.first_test: Re-read 4516 and 1206 at full resolution (check for red/press errors), then generate keystreams k[i]=(3301-p_i) mod 29 over consecutive primes and apply to both ct and the d-stream of chapter p15-22 with and without doublet-interrupter conventions.

hypotheses.title: The 272-entry base-62 table on p49-51 is a numeric key or index (one-time pad segment, prime indices, or book-cipher pointers) for the final chapters
hypotheses.motivation: Verified in p49.jpg/p50.jpg/p51.jpg: 11+14+9 rows x 8 cols of two-character groups, first char strictly 0-4 (values < ~310), embedded between rune paragraphs, terminated by the rare 10-dot red mark; it is entirely absent from krisyotam_runes.txt (only its surrounding 66/92 runes were transcribed), so it is community-underexploited by construction. Pages 41-48 each hold 271-274 runes — the same magnitude as 272 entries.
hypotheses.first_test: OCR the 272 values at full resolution, decode base-62, and profile them (range, repeats, deltas); then test as mod-29 keystream against ct and d-stream of ch.40-53, as prime indices, and as (page,word) or (line,position) pointers into the book itself.

hypotheses.title: Plaintext-preserving punctuation and literal numerals are crib anchors: quoted spans, apostrophe-S possessives, red list 1-5, and the standalone black '7' on p10 pass through the cipher unenciphered
hypotheses.motivation: Counted in the richer transcriptions and images: 10 quote characters (5 quoted spans) in p40-53.txt, 2 each in p3-7.txt and p15-22.txt, 4 apostrophes, '⁚' colons; red numerals 1-5 head list items on p36-38; a black numeral 7 stands as a one-character word on p10 line 8 (verified in image). The encipherer preserved word lengths, sentence dots, quotes and digits — each is a high-value positional crib (e.g., apostrophe-final words end in S; the word adjacent to '7' plausibly relates to counting).
hypotheses.first_test: Locate every quote/apostrophe/numeral at image level, record exact rune offsets, and run constrained crib-drag at those offsets under the rank-1 difference model (and under plain running-key models) using candidate words (SEVEN, NUMBER, PRIMES, names).

hypotheses.title: Glyph-template steganography audit: because the book is font-stamped, any single glyph deviating from its class template is a mark; the full book should be screened at pixel level
hypotheses.motivation: Measured: glyphs are digital stamps (150 pixel-identical same-shape pairs on p17; vine borders 0-pixel-different across 16 pages), so the noise floor is pure JPEG quantization; a hand-tweaked glyph, one-pixel shift, or weight change would be detectable and is currently uninspected. The deliberately BLURRED tree on p32 (only blurred object in the book) proves the authors manipulated render fidelity at least once.
hypotheses.first_test: Cluster all ~13k glyph bitmaps book-wide by class, compute per-instance Hamming distance to class centroid, and flag outliers beyond the JPEG-noise distribution; separately difference p32's tree against sharp tree art (p55 ghost tree, p14 sapling) to test whether the blur hides a second image.

hypotheses.title: The two red dot-mark types (13-dot vs 10-dot) are distinct structural operators, and the true section tree built from them (plus '&'/'$' markers) is a cipher boundary map
hypotheses.motivation: Measured red-component clustering across all 56 pages: the common mark has exactly 13 dots; a 10-dot variant occurs ONLY on p36, p38, p49 — precisely the numbered-list and table pages; krisyotam and the per-section txts conflate both into one symbol. 13 and 10 are themselves information (13 prime). Chapter marks '&' (18x) and '$' (9x) define a 9-10 chapter structure matching the margin-art stratigraphy.
hypotheses.first_test: Re-inventory every red mark at full res (dot count + geometry), rebuild the section tree, and re-run all stream statistics (doublets, IoC, diff distribution) per true section to see if any section behaves differently (e.g., a section where depletion is absent would localize a method change).

hypotheses.title: The 5-dot scatter on full-book page 73 is a pointer glyph (constellation or coordinate code) tied to the hex block above it
hypotheses.motivation: Measured from 73.jpg: five identical 69-70px dots at (1104,2448),(874,2517),(1604,2687),(922,2708),(1408,2748) — a W-like zigzag, same page as the 125-hex-digit block and the final cipher paragraph; the page is absent from the common p0-55 set entirely, so this art is nearly unexamined. The vine borders' fixed 3-dot and 5-dot clusters show the authors use dot-count vocabulary deliberately.
hypotheses.first_test: Normalize the 5 dot coordinates and compare pairwise-distance/angle signature against bright-5-star asterisms (Cassiopeia etc.) and against the book's other dot patterns; also test the coordinates as numbers (x,y deltas mod 29, concatenations against the hex block).

hypotheses.title: Mirror-level appended payloads are an unexhausted byte channel: LP 05.jpg's 336KB nibble-shifted numeric table and the 10.jpg/onion6.jpg concatenation
hypotheses.motivation: Verified bytes: cijhho123 LP 05.jpg has 336,713 trailing bytes that decode (after a one-nibble shift) to ASCII columns of numbers with '(' and '!' markers; 10.jpg ends with a complete second JPEG identical to onion6.jpg; TRAILING-DATA.json confirms only 13 of 1,208 scanned images carry trailing data, and REPORT-A.md documents that mirror pipelines STRIP such bytes (the 2012 imgur case) — so surviving appended data is precious and provenance-sensitive.
hypotheses.first_test: Fully decode 05.jpg's trailer with the one-nibble offset, reconstruct the table, and compare it against the p49-51 base-62 table, the p15 grid, and outguess-era payload formats; cross-check against 'A drop box of all unmodified files/2014onion7' to establish whether the trailer is original or a mirror addition.

hypotheses.title: Short anomalous segments (seg 54: 76 runes, 25 distinct, IoC 1.10) may be more weakly enciphered than the bulk and are the cheapest brute-force targets
hypotheses.motivation: Per-segment stats from krisyotam_runes.txt: seg 54 is the only cipher segment with normalized IoC above 1.09 and reduced alphabet (25/29); segs 49/50/52 are also short (66/92/179 runes) because they share pages with the table — and the segment-to-image alignment demonstrably breaks down after p49, meaning these segments' context (what sits beside them on the page) has been mis-modeled by every text-only attack.

lens: Veteran ARG/puzzle-designer reverse-engineering the author. The designer's established grammar (verified in this corpus, not from lore): teach primitives on easy pages (primes, totient, gematria prime-values, interrupters), then escalate self-referentially; sign everything with one key (137/140 VALID, exactly one fingerprint); and hide each stage's key INSIDE the already-released bytes — "The key has always been right in front of your eyes" (2012 signed msg, pgp/messages/2012-01-key-in-front-of-you.asc) is not a taunt, it is the design doctrine. I treated the 56 unsolved pages as the designer's artifact and asked: what process generated these exact statistics, and where would this specific author put the key so a careful solver could find it?
observations: THE core measurement: over the 13,041 cipher runes (krisyotam_runes.txt, 56 %-separated pages excluding the final plaintext page), rune unigrams are dead flat (29 counts in 400-493, normalized IoC 0.9998, flat on every single page), lag-2..250 coincidence rates are all at chance (3.0-3.7%), consecutive-rune differences mod 29 are flat for d=1..28 (406-515 each) — but d=0 (immediate repeats) occurs 89 times vs 453 expected: a 5x suppression, z≈-17. The suppression holds within words (0.63%), across word boundaries (0.83%), and on all 56 pages. This is the ONLY statistical structure in the entire stream.

That fingerprint is impossible for any cipher whose keystream is independent of the text: if ct=p+k with k independent, diff-0 stays ≈3.45%. I simulated plaintext-autokey, prime-autokey (ct_i=p_i+prime(p_{i-1})), totient-autokey, ciphertext-autokey, running-key English-on-English on English-in-runes text: all give diff-0 of 2.9-4.7%, never 0.7%. Whatever wrote these runes SAW its previous output symbol and avoided repeating it (feedback/rejection) — or the letters are not carrying the message at all. Doublet-avoidance is also the classic fingerprint of a HUMAN generating 'random' symbols by hand.

The word skeleton is English-shaped while the letters are not: 2,953 words, modal length 3, 3.4% one-letter words (English-like) — but the one-letter words use all 29 distinct runes (plain English allows only A/I), and repeated ciphertext words occur exactly at uniform-chance rate (15 repeated len-3 types vs ~11 expected from 731 draws over 29^3). So word boundaries are preserved plaintext structure; letter identities are statistically sterile.

The book's last page (segment 57) is UNENCIPHERED and I read it directly with the standard rune-letter map: 'PARABLE. LIKE THE INSTAR TUNNELING TO THE SURFACE. WE MUST SHED OUR OWN CIRCUMFERENCES. FIND THE DIVINITY WITHIN AND EMERGE.' The author closes the unsolved section with a plaintext imperative.

Verified-by-me stego precedent INSIDE this corpus: 'cijhho123/2014/Liber Primus/liber primus images full/05.jpg' carries 336,713 bytes after its JPEG EOI which are a byte-REVERSED valid 2400x3600 JPEG (the 'SOME WISDOM' page: red rubrics + 'THE PRIMES ARE SACRED / THE TOTIENT FUNCTION IS SACRED / ALL THINGS SHOULD BE ENCRYPTED'), and after the hidden JPEG's EOI sit 360 ASCII bytes: a 5x5 number grid (272 138 341 131 151 / 366 199 130 320 18 / 226 245 91 245 226 / 18 320 130 199 366 / 151 131 341 138 272) — every row sums to 1033 (3301 mirrored), and it is the explicit answer key equating the rune WORDS printed inside the page's magic square with their gematria prime-sum NUMBERS. The author personally demonstrated word<->number equivalence and hid the proof in trailing bytes.

The author's own signed statement of the key's location (pgp/messages/2016-01-liber-primus.asc, signature-verified corpus): 'Liber Primus is the way. Its words are the map, their meaning is the road, and their numbers are the direction.' Note 'direction' — and the only free parameter my statistics found is a stream of nonzero STEPS (directions) between consecutive runes.

Three distinct PGP-signed 991-byte blocks exist (signed-payloads/2014-01-liber-primus-hash-block*.bin), entropy 7.79-7.81 bits/byte, pairwise ~99% different, identical length; 991 is prime. They were released with an instruction mentioning 'the three magic squares'. Three same-size unexplained high-entropy objects are exactly what an encrypted final message (or three) would look like, waiting for a key.

Unenciphered Arabic numerals pass through the rune cipher: a literal '7' inline on page 10 (verified in page-images/p10.jpg, line 8, mid-sentence, next to a bare-tree marginal drawing), and red numerals 1-5 numbering a list across pages 36-38 (verified in p36.jpg: red '1', red 13-dot section mark). Numbers are plaintext leaks with known positions.

Rubrication channel mapped by pixel scan: 20/56 pages contain red ink; big red = chapter-opening words with giant dropcaps at pages 0,3,6,7,8,15,23,27,33,39,40,53,54 (chapter structure + crib-able titles); small red = a FIXED 13-dot diamond section ornament (13 components in 6 of 7 occurrences — not a data channel). The community transcription records none of this color information.

The signed 'interconnectedness' hex payload decodes byte-identical to the onion5 MP3 song (6,651,873 bytes, cmp IDENTICAL) — the author PGP-signed 6.6MB of audio; a 2013 signed message says 'knock on the sky and listen to the sound'. Audio is a first-class, author-attested carrier in this system.

Page marginalia from different pages stack into coherent composite drawings in a shared coordinate frame (Stacked Pages/The_map.jpg, Cadaver.jpg: trees, crosses, a lying body assembled from multiple pages) — cross-page spatial alignment is a designed degree of freedom.

Production forensics: full-dump images 00-16 lack the APP2/ICC segment present in 17-74 (two release batches); other release images carry trailing payloads too — onion6.jpg is appended inside 10.jpg (3.49MB), Huh2.jpg carries a 175KB reversed-JPEG trailer, and wiki-uncovering-cicada/images/Outt.png has 13,592 bytes after IEND that form a byte-palindrome built from a repeating 15-byte (120-bit) unit — an unexplained machine-readable object.

hypotheses.title: The cipher is output-feedback / chained: the message lives in the 13,040 nonzero STEPS between consecutive runes, not in the runes themselves
hypotheses.motivation: Measured on krisyotam_runes.txt: diffs mod 29 flat on 1..28, only diff-0 suppressed 5x (89 vs 453), all other lags clean — and I showed by simulation that NO independent-keystream cipher (random key, running key, prime/totient/plain autokey) reproduces this; the generator must see its previous output, i.e. each ciphertext rune is 'previous rune + a never-zero step'. The author's own signed 2016 words — 'their numbers are the DIRECTION' (pgp/messages/2016-01-liber-primus.asc) — name exactly this: a stream of directions/steps. The step alphabet has 28 values (1..28), suspiciously = 29-1 = totient of 29 ('THE TOTIENT FUNCTION IS SACRED', hidden wisdom page in 05.jpg).
hypotheses.first_test: Rebuild the stream as D[i] = (rune[i+1]-rune[i]) mod 29 ∈ {1..28} (per page, resetting at page breaks; keep word boundaries). Then (a) frequency/IoC analysis of D under 28-symbol assumption; (b) decrypt D with the already-taught keys: subtract totient-of-prime stream, prime stream, Fibonacci (note 'Fibbonachi.gif' sitting in the author-adjacent 2014 Liber Primus dump) mod 28 and mod 29, score for Gematria-English; (c) try D-1 ∈ {0..27} as a 28-letter alphabet (one rune dropped) against English frequencies.

lens: Historian of pre-computer hand ciphers (Trithemius to WW2 field practice). I judged everything by what a scribe can execute on paper at 13,000-rune scale: what table, what stream, what mechanical rule, what marginal apparatus. Answering the four questions: (1) The object is a 57-page hand-illuminated rune book: 56 pages of ciphertext whose statistics are flat (uniform singles, IoC=1.00/page, no periodicity, no cross-page key reuse) plus one final page in CLEAR runic English ("PARABLE... WE MUST SHED OUR OWN CIRCUMFERENCES") — i.e., a one-time-pad-grade presentation wrapped in medieval book conventions, with paragraph marks, section glyphs, red rubrication, and countable marginal devices exactly like a monastic scriptorium product. (2) What is odd: the ONLY statistical structure in 13,041 runes is a 5x suppression of adjacent identical runes (0.67% vs 3.45%); the book embeds non-runic machine-scale data (two pages of base62-looking byte grids, a PGP-signed 1005-byte hex block, byte-REVERSED JPEGs hidden after EOI markers); and the community transcription silently omits all of the non-runic apparatus. (3) First try: resolve whether the 88 doublets are transcription errors (making the no-doublet rule absolute), then per-page scans of the solved pages' own prime/totient stream family with per-page parameters and a skip-on-doublet rule. (4) What the material itself says the key is: the solved front pages used primes and totients; the hidden "SOME WISDOM" page (recovered here from the reversed trailer of 05.jpg) teaches that rune-words and their prime-gematria sums are interchangeable inside a 1033 magic square (1033 = 3301 reversed) — the book is telling you the key lives in the prime-value domain and that reversal is an operation it uses; the untranscribed marginalia (berry dots, red numerals, red arrow) are the most likely carriers of per-page parameters.
observations: Transcription structure: /tmp/lp_blind/material/krisyotam_runes.txt holds 57 %-separated pages; page 56 decodes by DIRECT Gematria letter mapping to plaintext ('PARABLE. LICE THE INSTAR TUNNELNG TO THE SURFACE...'), IoC 1.82, while all 56 other pages sit at IoC ~1.00 (range 0.93-1.10). The file also contains non-rune symbols &: 18, $: 9, digits 1-5 and 7, and a final section mark.

The single statistical anomaly: over 13,041 cipher runes, adjacent identical runes occur 88 times = 0.67% vs 3.45% random expectation, while single-rune frequencies are perfectly uniform (chi2 25.6, df 28), kappa is flat for shifts 1-60, consecutive-line and cross-page same-position coincidence are exactly random (3.457% vs 3.45% over 315,779 comparisons), and lagged difference/sum distributions are uniform at every lag 2-40. The first-difference distribution is uniform EXCEPT the hole at zero.

Simulation discrimination (my own code, English text mapped to 29 runes): plaintext doublet rate 3.33%; encryption with the solved-page phi(prime) stream gives 3.51% doublets (does NOT reproduce the hole); plaintext autokey gives non-uniform singles chi2 715 (ruled out by observed 25.6); a random stream with a skip-on-doublet rule gives 0.00% doublets with uniform singles (chi2 22) - the only family matching all observed statistics, implying the 88 observed doublets are lapses or transcription errors.

Doublet exceptions are page-clustered: pages 19, 24, 27, 29, 44 carry 4-5 doublets each (1.4-2.1%), while 20 pages have zero; the numbered-list pages 37-38 have exactly zero. Doubled runes span 26 of 29 letters (no single interrupter rune explains them).

Onion pages 50 and 51 (released-artifacts/Hadyn_cicada/2014/ky2khlqdf7qdznac.onion/50.jpg, 51.jpg) carry grids of two-character alphanumeric pairs, 8 per row (~14 + 9 rows, ~184 values), first character always 0-4. Base62 decoding yields near-uniform values, min 0, max ~262, mean 132.6, 95.5% below 256 - statistically indistinguishable from ~184 random BYTES (~1472 bits). These grids are COMPLETELY ABSENT from krisyotam_runes.txt.

Hidden reversed payloads: 05.jpg ('liber primus images full') carries 336,713 bytes after the JPEG EOI which, when byte-REVERSED, become a valid 2400x3600 JPEG pixel-identical to page-images/0_wisdom.jpg, plus an ASCII block giving a 5x5 square (272 138 341 131 151 / 366 199 130 320 18 / 226 245 91 245 226 / ...) whose every row sums to 1033 = 3301 reversed. On the page itself the square MIXES Arabic numbers with rune-words standing in for the missing values - an explicit lesson that words and their prime-gematria sums are interchangeable. 10.jpg and ONION_2_JPG.jpg also carry appended full-page JPEGs (TRAILING-DATA.json, verified from bytes).

Red Arabic numerals 1,2,3,4,5 mark a five-item list spanning pages 36-38 (verified in both transcription and scans), there is an inline numeral 7 inside cipher text on transcription page 10, and a cuneiform-looking emblem recurs at the bottom of page 33 and the top of pages 36-37 - three separate non-runic intrusions into the rune system.

Untranscribed marginalia exist across the unsolved section: branch/root border drawings carry 'berry' dot clusters that vary per page in BOTH count and fill (page 50 left branch: 2 filled + 2 hollow dots; right branch: 5 filled), page 53 has an in-text RED upward arrow and double-prime (quote-like) marks, page 33 has a row of three large black dots. None of this is recorded in the transcription.
Page 32's tree illustration is deliberately Gaussian-blurred - the only blurred element in an otherwise crisp, vector-like book.

Machine-crypto companions: 2014-01-liber-primus-hash-block.asc is a PGP-signed 1005-byte hex blob released alongside the LP onion (signed by the single verified key 7A35090F per SIGNATURES.json: 137/140 files VALID, exactly one signing key ever); it remains uninterpreted and is a candidate verification oracle for any claimed solution.

Word apparatus is real but letter-keying is per-position: 2,953 cipher words, modal length 3, mean 4.4 (English-like); 100 one-rune words spread over ALL 29 runes nearly uniformly (English would allow only a/i: so the key varies within words, ruling out word-keyed monoalphabets); gematria word sums show NO prime bias (21.2% prime vs 20.8% shuffled baseline) and uniform residues mod 29.

Mirror integrity problems in the primary corpus: the Hadyn onion dump is missing 6.jpg-9.jpg entirely, 54.jpg is truncated (bottom two-thirds grey, 103 bytes unprocessed), and the 2015 '1033adacic' artifacts resolve to a zenbox.pl hosting placeholder with no PGP signature - the 1033 tie-in notwithstanding, they are likely inauthentic and should not drive analysis.

hypotheses.title: The cipher is an additive stream with a mechanical NO-DOUBLET rule (skip/bump the key when the output would repeat the previous rune)
hypotheses.motivation: The only structure in 13,041 runes is the d=0 hole: doublets 0.67% vs 3.45%, with uniform singles (chi2 25.6), uniform lagged diffs/sums everywhere else, and no periodicity. My simulations show this signature is NOT produced by the solved-page phi(prime) stream (3.51% doublets) nor by autokey (breaks singles uniformity), but IS produced exactly by any stream cipher plus a skip-on-repeat scribal rule (0% doublets, uniform everything). Such a rule is hand-practical (a one-glance check per rune) and silently defeats Kasiski/kappa because skips desynchronize any underlying period - explaining 11 unsolved years with classical statistics looking 'random'.
hypotheses.first_test: Locate all 88 doublet sites (pages 19/24/27/29/44 hold 23 of them) in the 2400x3600 scans and re-read each glyph pair: if most are transcription errors, the rule is absolute. Then re-run periodicity searches under an insertion-tolerant alignment (DP/HMM that models occasional key-skips), since a SHORT repeating key + skip rule is no longer excluded by the flat kappa.

hypotheses.title: Unsolved pages continue the solved pages' prime/totient stream family with per-page parameters (start index, direction, affine constant, interrupter), one key per page

Measured: zero keystream reuse across pages (3.457% cross-page coincidence = random) and page-level heterogeneity in doublet behavior, so each page is independently keyed; the hidden SOME WISDOM page (recovered from 05.jpg's reversed trailer) explicitly sanctifies primes and gematria values; prime-derived streams are the only hand-computable non-repeating streams the authors demonstrably used.

hypotheses.title: The base62 pair-grids on pages 50-51 are a ~184-byte machine-crypto object (key material, hash, or encrypted payload) - the book's bridge out of the hand-cipher domain, and currently invisible to anyone working from the transcription
hypotheses.motivation: Measured from the scans: ~184 two-char groups, first char always 0-4, decoding under the standard 0-9A-Za-z base62 alphabet to near-uniform values with mean 132.6 and 95.5% below 256 - the distribution of random bytes, not of gematria word-sums (English word-sums measured mean 172, max 451). These grids appear in NO form in krisyotam_runes.txt, so every purely-transcription-based attack of the last decade has ignored ~1,472 bits of deliberately placed data.

hypotheses.title: Reversal is an operational motif: run the best stream candidates over the text read backwards (whole page, whole book, or boustrophedon by line)
hypotheses.motivation: Demonstrated in the material three independent ways: the hidden page in 05.jpg is stored as a byte-REVERSED JPEG; its magic square sums to 1033 = 3301 reversed; and Atbash (alphabet reversal) was already one of the solved pages' ciphers. An entity this fond of reversal plausibly applies it to reading order or key direction - a zero-cost hand operation invisible to forward-only statistics (all my forward stats are direction-symmetric except the doublet rule, which survives reversal).
hypotheses.first_test: Re-run the full H2 scan suite on (a) each page's rune sequence reversed, (b) line-boustrophedon readings, and (c) forward text with key stream indices descending from an unknown start; the scoring harness is identical, so this doubles H2's search space cheaply.

hypotheses.title: The untranscribed marginalia (berry-dot counts and fills, red arrow, dot rows, section glyphs) encode per-page key parameters
hypotheses.motivation: Measured on the scans: branch borders carry dot clusters differing per page in count AND fill (50.jpg left: 2 filled + 2 hollow; right: 5 filled; 53.jpg differs), page 53 has an in-text red up-arrow and double-prime marks, page 33 a row of three large dots - all absent from the transcription. hypotheses.first_test: Census every page: count and position every non-rune mark (filled dots, hollow dots, arrows, primes, emblems) into a table; test the resulting per-page numbers directly as H2 start-indices/offsets, and check correlations with page length and position in the book.

lens: data-archaeologist: raw bytes, containers, encodings, and machine-measurable statistics of the Liber Primus corpus, examined blind
observations: WHAT THE OBJECT IS (byte level): the canonical release is 75 JPEGs, every one exactly 2400x3600 (cijhho123/2014/Liber Primus/liber primus images full/00-74.jpg). The 2014 onion mirror (Hadyn_cicada/2014/ky2khlqdf7qdznac.onion/) maps as onion/N == cij/(N+17) byte-identically; the onion dump is MISSING files 6-9 (= cij 23-26) and 55-57, and its 54.jpg is truncated at exactly 212992 bytes = 52*4096 (verified: no FFD9, and it is the exact prefix of cij/71.jpg) - a mirror-download artifact, not a puzzle.

THE ONE STATISTICAL ANOMALY IN THE TEXT: over the 54 cipher pages of krisyotam_runes.txt (12,880 runes), adjacent-equal runes occur 85 times vs 444 expected for uniform (5.2x suppressed, p astronomically small). Every other test is EXACTLY uniform-random: unigram chi2 25.6 (df 28), equality at lags 2-12 all ~1/29 (437-476 vs 444 expected), lag-1 sum distribution flat, repeated 4/5-gram counts match random expectation, and the lag-1 difference stream has IoC 1.0245 which is fully explained by the missing-zero cell alone. The ciphertext is indistinguishable from a one-time pad EXCEPT that c[i+1]==c[i] almost never happens. The runes that DO double are uniformly spread over all 29 values (max 7 occurrences of any one), and the suppression is even across all 54 pages (0-5 doublets per page).

A 0.5%-PROBABILITY REPEAT: the only repeated 7-gram in 13,041 runes (expected count under random ~0.005 at L=7) is the two-word phrase 'ᛞᛄᚢ-ᛒᛖᛁ' with IDENTICAL word boundaries, at page 27 offset 28 (image cij/44.jpg) and page 54 offset 70 (image cij/71.jpg, the short tree-flanked 'spell' page); the 7th matching rune crosses into page 55. Gap = 6395 = 5 x 1279. I crib-tested extended keystream sharing by aligning the two pages at the repeat: difference-stream IoC over 214 aligned pairs is 1.023 vs 0.965 control - no extended sharing, so it is either coincidence or an isolated enciphered-phrase repeat.

WORD STRUCTURE IS REAL: 3,367 words, mean length 3.90, length histogram English-like (1:324, 2:635, 3:798, 4:566, 5:356...), zero repeated words of length>=4 (random predicts 0.18) and 13 repeated 3-letter words (random predicts 10.7). So word boundaries carry plaintext information but word tokens are position-dependent ciphertext.

HIDDEN CONTAINER IN cij/05.jpg: after the page's EOI at byte 336353 sits reverse(host JPEG + 360 chars of ASCII hex). The reversed blob is byte-identical to the host page image itself, and the hex tail decodes to a 5x5 number square: rows [272 138 341 131 151 / 366 199 130 320 18 / 226 245 91 245 226 / 18 320 130 199 366 / 151 131 341 138 272]. Every row, column and diagonal sums to 1033; the square is 180-degree rotationally symmetric with center 91. The 2015 follow-on domains in this same corpus are literally named '1033adacic.{cf,ga,ml,gq}' (released-artifacts/2015-1033/).

THE RELEASE USES FILE CONCATENATION AS A MOTIF: cij/01.jpg has 02.jpg appended (02.jpg's full 175,159 bytes are 01.jpg's trailer); cij/10.jpg (4.2MB) contains 11.jpg, 12.jpg and 13.jpg appended in sequence; plus the reversed blob in 05.jpg. TRAILING-DATA.json scanned 1208 images and found 13 with trailers but lists 9 'unparseable' images never characterized.

SIGNED, NEVER-DECRYPTED PAYLOADS: cijhho123/2014/additional docs/outguss/ holds Cicada-signed outguess payloads. Three of them ('intus', 'liber primus', 'runes') are hex blobs that each decode to EXACTLY 991 bytes (a prime), entropy 7.79-7.81 - three equal-length, still-opaque ciphertext blocks. A fourth ('liber primus 5') says 'Let the text guide you. Good luck. 3301' followed by hex of the same hidden-JPEG material as the 05.jpg trailer.

A COLOR CHANNEL THE TRANSCRIPTION DROPS: red-pixel scan of all 75 originals shows ~30 pages carry red ink: red Arabic numerals 1-5 marking a five-item list spanning cij/53-55 (transcription pages 36-38; verified visually), red drop-caps (big red ᛗ on cij/44, red ᚠ on cij/71), red first-lines/phrases ending in red ⁘ marks, and tiny red marks (3-15 px) on pages 15,19,31,39,43,49,53,66,72. krisyotam_runes.txt records the digits ('1'-'5', one '7' inline on page 10) but NOT which runes are red; its '&'/'$' symbols at page ends mark illustrations (wing/cicada/tree glyphs).

END MATTER: transcription page 56 is direct unenciphered runeglish ('parable. like the instar tunneling to the surface. we must shed our own circumferences. find the divinity within and emerge.' + a '§' end glyph), while the short pages 49-55 immediately before it are still flat-IoC cipher (IoC 0.83-1.10). Page 54's full-page layout is a red drop-cap block flanked by two rooted trees.

hypotheses.title: The unsolved pages use a chained/correlated keystream in the same family as the solved prime-totient stream - the lag-1 doublet suppression is its fingerprint

An independent random key cannot produce this.

The matching family defines the search space; then brute-force seeds/offsets per page scoring on doublet rate + crib 'ᚦᛖ'.

lens: Adversarial reframer: assume the community has misclassified the OBJECT ITSELF. Everyone treats the 56 unsolved pages as "a ciphertext of an English message awaiting the right classical attack." I spent the session measuring what the material actually is: 13,041 runes whose every statistic is machine-flat EXCEPT one glaring human-shaped anomaly, wrapped in a book that lavishes effort on the SHAPE of language (word lengths, sentences, rubrics, numbered lists) while containing zero token-level language structure, delivered through a channel that demonstrably hid payloads in file bytes rather than page pixels. What is this object? Possibly not a text at all: a delta-tape, a one-share secret, a hand-made noise carrier for marked subsets, or a filter designed to consume solvers. What does the material say the key is? If anything, it says the key is NOT in the rune stream: the only in-band plaintext (final page, which I decoded myself: "PARABLE. LIKE THE INSTAR TUNNELING TO THE SURFACE. WE MUST SHED OUR OWN CIRCUMFERENCES. FIND THE DIVINITY WITHIN AND EMERGE.") points inward/elsewhere, the WISDOM grid page is an explicit key-like numeral table, and the corpus's own 2017 signed pastebin says "Beware false paths."
observations: THE anomaly (my central measurement): adjacent-identical runes occur at 0.64% within words and 0.83% across word boundaries vs 3.45% expected for the otherwise-perfectly-flat stream (88 doublets where ~450 are expected; ~15 sigma). Every other lag 1-250 is normal (range 2.99-3.99%). Measured on krisyotam_runes.txt, 13,041 cipher runes, pages 0-55. No properly-keyed additive/poly-alphabetic cipher produces this; it is the signature of a generation process that avoids immediate repeats.

The difference stream c[i+1]-c[i] mod 29 is uniform over 1..28 (each 3.10-3.97%) with 0 suppressed, and the SECOND difference has IC 1.0004 (perfectly flat). The corpus is statistically exactly 'a random walk on a 29-wheel with nonzero steps' - i.e., a cumulative sum of a nonzero stream.

Word-token repetition exactly matches iid-random chance: L=2 words 118 collisions vs 136 expected, L=3 17 vs 11, L>=4 0 observed vs ~0.2 expected (2,973 words). No Zipf, no function-word echo. This kills every cipher in which a ciphertext word is a function of the plaintext word alone (monoalphabetic, Atbash, shift, any word-restarting Vigenere) - which is exactly the method family that solved the first 15 pages.

Yet the SHAPE of language is meticulously simulated: word-length distribution mean 4.42/mode 3 (the genuine English final page measures mean 4.75), 221 'sentences' of 1-52 words (mean 13.4), paragraphs, 13 red drop-cap section openings (pages 0,3,6,7,8,15,23,27,33,39,40,53,54 - measured by red-pixel scan of all p*.jpg), 7 red dotted-grid section-end stamps, a numbered list with red European digits 1-5 on pages 36-38, a three-dot asterism on p33, a cuneiform-like glyph cluster at p33-bottom/p37-top, and a full RED paragraph on p53 followed by a cicada drawing.

Monogram distribution dead flat (29 runes each 3.05-3.75%, IC_29=0.9998; bigram entropy 9.643/9.716 max) and homogeneous across the book (first-half vs second-half chi2=31.9, df=28). Flat and driftless like a machine - but doublet-suppressed like a human. That tension is the single most under-examined fact in the material.
The doublet suppression is uniform: spread over 43 of 56 pages and over all 28 rune identities (max 7 for any rune). One process generated the entire unsolved corpus.

The final (57th) block in the transcription is direct-mapping PLAINTEXT - I decoded it myself with the standard futhorc mapping: 'PARABLE. LIKE THE INSTAR TUNNELING TO THE SURFACE. WE MUST SHED OUR OWN CIRCUMFERENCES. FIND THE DIVINITY WITHIN AND EMERGE.' The one page the authors wrote in clear is an instruction pointing away from the text.

0_wisdom.jpg is not prose: a 'WISDOM' heading plus a 5x5 table mixing arabic numerals (272,138,131,151,18,226,245,...) with rune words, numerals placed with 180-degree rotational symmetry (top row 272,138,_,131,151; bottom row 151,131,_,138,272). Note: page 22 of the cipher text contains exactly 131 runes and 272/273 are the modal full-page rune counts - untested coincidence.

The delivery channel hides payloads in file bytes, measured in TRAILING-DATA.json and verified by me on disk: liber-primus-full 05.jpg carries 336,713 bytes of structured ASCII-digit columns after EOI; 10.jpg carries a complete second 3.4MB JPEG; the SIGNED onion5 liber-primus jpg carries 10,923 trailing bytes (its own JFIF); the 2012 final image ends with the 61-byte plaintext trailer 'TIBERIVS CLAVDIVS CAESAR says ...' (a Caesar-shifted URL). signed-payloads/ also contains a PGP-SIGNED 'liber-primus-hash-block.bin' plus two signed outguess payloads - the entity attested hashes/blobs for this book out-of-band.

Negative results worth recording: gematria-primus word-sum primality matches shuffled control (0.212 vs 0.203-0.216); page gematria sums mostly composite; kappa periodicity flat to lag 250 (max 3.99% at lag 99); no page-level IC outlier except the tiny pages (p49=66 runes, IC 0.825). Line lengths are hand-justified 20-24 runes; pages are 12-13 lines; sections end mid-page like a real book.

The transcription itself is lossy in a way that matters for object-classification: the page images distinguish at least two separators (triple-dot word-stop vs red dot-GRID section stamp, with varying dot counts) that krisyotam_runes.txt collapses to '.'; marginal art contains deliberate small dot clusters (seen in p54/p55 vine borders). The community's canonical text throws away every non-rune mark.

The corpus's own signed 2017 pastebin (released-artifacts/2016-2017/pastebin_yEiTHhvF.txt): 'Beware false paths. Always verify PGP signature from 7A35090F' - and REPORT-A.md records 137 valid signatures from exactly one key, with the Internet Archive's copy of a key 2012 artifact having been silently stripped by an image pipeline. Provenance of each individual LP page against the signed hash block is therefore checkable and, as far as this material shows, unchecked.

hypotheses.title: It is a delta-tape, not a text: the message (if any) lives in the DIFFERENCES between consecutive runes; the runes are the cumulative readout of a walk on the 29-wheel
hypotheses.motivation: Measured: diff stream uniform over 1..28 with 0 suppressed (0.67%), second difference perfectly flat (IC 1.0004) - the exact signature of c[i]=c[i-1]+s[i] with nonzero steps s. The community attacks the runes; nobody attacks the step stream as the primary object. The one plaintext page even says 'shed our own CIRCUMFERENCES' - movement on a circle. Also explains why the first-15-pages methods (which operate on rune values) all died at page 15: the object class changed.
hypotheses.first_test: Re-express all 56 pages as the step stream s[i] in 1..28 (keep word/sentence/section boundaries), then run the full classical battery ON THE STEPS: IC at all periods, Vigenere/autokey trials with 28-letter alphabet, prime/totient stream subtraction, and crucially test whether step values correlate with word boundaries (e.g., steps at word-initial positions distributed differently). Takes an afternoon; the stream is already extracted in my scratch code.

hypotheses.title: It is one share of a two-share secret: a hand-generated one-time pad (or the XOR-half of a payload) whose other half was never published or is a physical/out-of-band object - standalone-unsolvable BY DESIGN
hypotheses.motivation: Flat monograms, flat kappa to lag 250, zero word-token repeats = key at least as long as the book. The lag-1 doublet suppression is then the HUMAN fingerprint of whoever generated the pad by hand (humans under-produce immediate repeats) - the only explanation I found that reconciles 'genuinely keyed' with 'statistically impossible for a sound cipher'. The corpus habitually splits content across channels: signed hash-block.bin, signed outguess payloads, 05.jpg's 336KB digit trailer, 10.jpg's appended JPEG - all measured in this material.
hypotheses.first_test: Mod-29 subtract the rune stream against every >=13k-symbol byte stream already in the corpus (05.jpg digit trailer, 10.jpg trailing JPEG, the signed hash-block.bin, interconnectedness mp3 PCM, the 2014 onion dump bytes) under a few natural mappings, and test residuals for English IC. Simultaneously, compare the doublet-suppression profile against published human random-generation data (humans also over-alternate at specific lags) vs PRNGs.

hypotheses.title: It is a filter/initiation instrument, not a message: human-crafted whitened filler whose function is to consume and select solvers (the content is the solver's own transformation)
hypotheses.motivation: Three measurements point here: (a) the 15-sigma human-style doublet suppression with otherwise machine-flat, drift-free statistics; (b) word-collision counts matching iid chance EXACTLY (no latent message structure at any word granularity); (c) the only clear text in the book is an instruction that the payload is internal: 'WE MUST SHED OUR OWN CIRCUMFERENCES. FIND THE DIVINITY WITHIN AND EMERGE.' The enormous care spent on language-SHAPE (word lengths, sentences, rubrics, numbered lists) without language-STATISTICS is exactly what a liturgical prop needs and exactly what a real ciphertext does not.
hypotheses.first_test: Falsification drive: fit a maximum-likelihood 'human pseudorandom generator' model (symbol-inhibition-of-recency over lags 1-5 + motor/keyboard-adjacency bias for whatever input method) and test whether it fully explains the corpus; separately hunt for ANY residual structure it cannot produce (cross-page correlations, section-boundary effects). If the human-noise model is sufficient statistics, the message hypothesis loses its last anomaly.

hypotheses.title: It is a carrier with a marked payload (grille-class): only the RED/marked elements are message; the 13k black runes are cover
hypotheses.motivation: Measured red-ink structure across all 56 scans: 13 red drop-caps + red opening words, a FULL red paragraph on p53 immediately before the cicada colophon, red dot-grid stamps whose dot counts vary, red numerals 1-5, three oversized dots on p33, a repeated cuneiform-like glyph cluster (p33 bottom, p37 top), and dot triplets hidden in the p54/p55 vine borders. hypotheses.first_test: Build the complete 'marked-element transcription' from the images: every red rune in book order, every dot-grid's dot count, the asterism, the glyph clusters, border-dot positions.
